//: The public export surface of @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext (0.12), and the source of truth for it.
Edited by hand; `npm run generate:exports` renders it into pkg/ts/index.ts and into the export test in
each test-consumer fixture. `npm run check:exports` fails the build when any of the three drifts.
`blocks` is emitted in order and reproduces index.ts exactly, comments included, so this file is the
only place a new export is declared. `kind` is the runtime typeof a consumer must find; `array` and
`object` are distinguished because typeof cannot tell them apart, and `member` / `element` reach one
level in, since `typeof CONTRACT_VERSIONS === 'object'` would pass for any object at all.
`dummies` carries one sample value per exported type, emitted verbatim into the generated tests and
checked by each fixture's own tsc. The types are NOT re-described here: TypeScript already describes
them in pkg/ts/types/public.ts, and a JSON mirror of those fields would be a second definition free to
drift. A sample value costs one line and catches a renamed or removed FIELD, which a bare type binding
cannot. Order is dependency-first — the generated bindings reference each other — and is therefore
independent of the export order in `blocks`. Every type-only export must appear exactly once here.
A `dummy` is emitted verbatim, so write it as an array of lines whenever `const dummyX: X = <dummy>;`
would pass 120 columns. `prettier:check` fails the build if it does.
This generation's surface is NOT v13's, and the differences are the point: no `updateV12ToV13`, no KMS
context calls, `KMSVerifierInitConfig` still carries the signer set and threshold that 0.13 moves to
`ProtocolConfig`, and `VerifyExpectations.kmsThreshold` is scalar rather than the four v13 splits it
into. A sample copied across generations would compile against the wrong shape.

comment: The deterministic-deployment counterpart: addresses that depend on nothing but the factory, the salt
inputs and the init code — no deployer nonce, so they survive any transaction that moves it.
Installs a standing `ACLOwner` over an EOA-owned ACL. Exposed because the next generation's
update flow requires a live stack's ACL to already be owned by an `ACLOwner`.
Emergency pause / unpause of the ACL, driven through the standing `ACLOwner` by its admin.
The `getVersion()` string every contract in this generation reports. Generated from the contracts
themselves (internal/generateContractVersions.ts), so it cannot drift from what a deployed stack
answers — which is what makes it usable as the expected value when verifying a deployment.
Full-integrity verification of a deployed or upgraded stack. `snapshotStack` is taken BEFORE an
upgrade; `verify` compares against it, so "nothing else changed" is checkable rather than assumed.

comment: The gateway the cleartext stack is bootstrapped against. Decided in `sdk/cleartext-config.json` and
copied here byte-for-byte (rule 23), so a consumer that needs these — the hardhat plugin builds its
EIP-712 domain from them — reads the source of truth instead of transcribing it. A transcription is
how the plugin came to hold a stale gateway chain id, which made every input-proof signature recover
to a junk address.
